ranking.rationale: Age is one of the most robust and causally relevant predictors of hypertension, with strong stable signal across states, years, and demographic groups. It is less likely than state, year, race, or socioeconomic proxies to act mainly as a domain identifier, and offers larger marginal value than narrower comorbidity or lifestyle indicators as a first feature.

Diabetes is a strong, semantically causal comorbidity/risk factor for hypertension and should remain predictive across domains beyond age, unlike state/year identifiers or more brittle socioeconomic and reporting artifacts.

Physical inactivity is a well-established, semantically stable risk factor for hypertension and adds complementary lifestyle signal beyond age and diabetes. It is more transportable across domains than state, year, race, employment, or missingness indicators, and less brittle than access-to-care or cancer-history variables.

Sex is a well-established, semantically stable predictor of hypertension risk that adds complementary signal beyond age, diabetes, and physical activity. It is less likely than state, year, race, employment, or missingness indicators to encode domain shifts or brittle shortcuts.

Poverty captures socioeconomic stress and access-related risk that is plausibly and stably associated with hypertension across domains, while adding information not already covered by age, diabetes, physical activity, and sex. It is less likely than state, year, race, employment, or missingness indicators to act as a domain identifier or brittle shortcut.

Physical inactivity is a well-established, semantically stable risk factor for hypertension and complements age, diabetes, sex, and poverty without relying on domain identifiers or demographic shortcuts. This adds robust lifestyle signal while avoiding brittle features like state, year, race, or missingness indicators.

Cost-related inability to see a doctor is a stable socioeconomic/health-access signal that remains semantically linked to hypertension risk across domains. It adds information beyond age, diabetes, sex, poverty, and physical activity, while avoiding obvious domain identifiers like state/year and more brittle demographic shortcuts like race.

Adds complementary access-to-care signal beyond poverty: inability to afford needed medical care is stably associated with undiagnosed or poorly controlled hypertension and should generalize better than state, year, race, or missingness indicators. It is also more directly health-related than employment, diet, alcohol, smoking, or cancer history given the features already selected.

Smoking history is a well-established, semantically stable cardiovascular risk factor that adds health-behavior signal beyond age, sex, diabetes, poverty, medical-cost access, and physical activity. It is more transportable than state, year, race, employment, or missingness indicators, and less brittle than many cancer-history or survey-artifact features.

Adds complementary smoking-risk information beyond ever-smoked status: distinguishing never smokers from former/current smokers is a stable, semantically relevant predictor for hypertension, while avoiding brittle domain-ID features like state or year and weaker shortcut demographics.

Alcohol consumption is a plausible, semantically stable behavioral risk factor for hypertension that adds complementary lifestyle signal beyond age, diabetes, exercise, smoking, sex, and poverty, while avoiding obvious domain-ID features like state/year and shortcut-heavy demographics.

Vegetable consumption adds a broadly causal, behavior-linked signal for hypertension risk that should transfer across domains better than state, year, race, or missingness indicators. It is also complementary to already selected age, diabetes, smoking, alcohol, exercise, sex, and poverty features, improving lifestyle-risk coverage without relying on brittle domain identifiers.

Vegetable intake adds a plausible, semantically stable lifestyle signal for hypertension risk that complements age, diabetes, activity, smoking, alcohol, poverty, and sex. It is less likely than state, year, race, employment, or missingness indicators to encode domain shifts or brittle shortcuts, and it is the informative counterpart to the already selected low-vegetable category.

Binge drinking adds a stable cardiovascular-behavior risk signal beyond total alcohol volume, age, sex, diabetes, smoking, activity, diet, and poverty. It is more semantically tied to blood-pressure risk than state/year or demographic shortcut features, and likely generalizes better across domains than employment, race, or missingness indicators.

Fruit intake adds a broadly causal lifestyle signal for hypertension risk that should transfer across domains. It complements already selected exercise, vegetable intake, smoking, alcohol, diabetes, age, sex, and socioeconomic variables with relatively low leakage risk, while state/year, race, missingness indicators, and many employment categories are more likely to encode domain or brittle artifacts.

Unable-to-work employment status adds stable health-related signal beyond age, poverty, and access variables, capturing disability/chronic illness burden strongly linked to hypertension while avoiding explicit domain identifiers like state/year and weaker missingness artifacts.

Current smoking status adds stable cardiovascular risk information beyond lifetime smoking, alcohol, diet, activity, age, sex, diabetes, and SES. The 'every day' smoking category is semantically tied to hypertension risk and is more transportable than state, year, race, missingness, or cancer-history features, which are more likely to encode domain or brittle artifacts.

Adds the missing complementary level of fruit consumption, a broadly causal lifestyle correlate of hypertension risk that should transfer across domains. It provides stable incremental signal beyond age, diabetes, activity, smoking, alcohol, poverty, and sex, while avoiding brittle domain identifiers like state/year and weaker shortcut features like race or missingness indicators.

Current smoking status adds stable cardiovascular risk information beyond lifetime smoking and smoking frequency already selected; the 'not at all' category is especially informative for blood pressure while being less domain-identifying than state, year, race, or missingness indicators.

Adds the key smoking-status contrast (some-days smoking) beyond lifetime smoking and daily smoking already selected; smoking behavior is a stable cardiovascular risk factor and more semantically predictive than state, year, race, missingness, or brittle administrative indicators.
